evidence.quote: A variant of dialectal {{m|en|scranny|t=thin; lean; scraggy; poor; scanty; of inferior quality}}, perhaps from {{der|en|non|skran|t=rubbish; junk}} {{suffix|en||y}}. Compare {{cog|no|skran|t=lean, thin, skinny}}, {{cog|en|scrannel|t=lean; meager; poor; worthless}}. Alternatively, perhaps from {{der|en|non|skrælna||to be shrivelled}}.<ref>{{R:Online Etymology Dictionary|scrawny}}</ref>
"meager, wasted, raw-boned," 1824, apparently a dialectal variant of scranny "lean, thin"… See origin and meaning of scrawny. from a Scandinavian source, perhaps Old Norse skrælna "to shrivel.
